question: When does a wider network help?
finding: Widening the high-resolution branch of an HRNet improved the validation score on the PARM promoter MPRA and made little difference on the Gosai MPRA. The two models started from different widths, trained on different assays and scored different targets.
exception: Widening is not one intervention. On the Gosai MPRA, widening the final shared stage of a dilated residual network lowered the score.
coverage: These are selected comparisons from two searches, not every width experiment they ran. Each one compares a single run with its recorded parent, at one seed, so seed-to-seed variation is not estimated.
reading: Each change is shown in its own study's metric. PARM reports R² per fragment and Gosai reports mean R² across three cell types, so the sizes of the changes are not on one scale. Compare directions and each change against its own study's threshold.
The threshold is what each study treated as a meaningful change. It is not an uncertainty interval.
All scores here are validation scores, which the searches used to choose models. Where a study also recorded a held-out test score for both runs, it is shown under Details.

next.hypothesis: Widening may help more when weight sharing limits the number of independently learned filters.
next.test: Vary width at the same stage in otherwise matched weight-tied and untied models, repeat each comparison across seeds, and record the added training cost. Repeating that design on a second task would test whether the rule transfers.

groups.title: Same branch in related architectures
groups.note: Both studies widened the highest-resolution branch of an HRNet, an architecture that keeps features at several resolutions.

Widen the HRNet full-resolution branch from 96 to 128 channels

groups.title: Widening elsewhere in the network
groups.note: These change a different part of the network, so they answer a different question. They help mark how far the result above reaches.

comparisons.change: Widen the deeper stages of a pyramid whose reverse-complement weight sharing halves its independently learned filters (192 to 256 and 256 to 320 channels)
comparisons.note: A different architecture, and a different reason for adding capacity: the weight sharing leaves each layer half its nominal number of free filters.
